name: Fully Automated Luxury Communism
summary: Fully automated luxury communism, set out by Aaron Bastani in his 2019 manifesto and earlier writing, holds that automation, renewable energy, asteroid mining, gene editing and cellular agriculture are creating extreme supply that capitalism's profit logic cannot absorb. Its goal is a post-work, post-scarcity communism in which luxury is available to all, work is largely automated and what is automated is commonly owned. Its stated route is a reformist, electoral path built on universal basic services, public ownership, municipal and public banking and worker-owned firms, not a Leninist revolution, and it rejects green calls for austerity and degrowth.
scope: This profile covers Aaron Bastani's FALC as the defining sources present it: his 2019 book Fully Automated Luxury Communism: A Manifesto, his 2015 and 2019 interviews and his Novara Media writing, as quoted and reviewed in scholarly and reference reviews. The defining sources (Radical Philosophy, Society and Space and other reviews) treat the book as the main statement of the idea, and the 2015 Guardian piece traces the slogan to Plan C's 'Luxury for All'. It excludes the wider accelerationist, post-work and eco-modernist literatures and Plan C's own views except where the defining sources tie them to FALC.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Bastani lists universally guaranteed healthcare among the demands of FALC.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Bastani rejects the claim that 'the market always knows best' and argues that technology could distribute goods more efficiently than markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Bastani's stated demand is 'the full automation of everything and common ownership of that which is automated', and he calls for seizing the means of production and for municipally provided services without a profit motive.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bastani calls for common ownership of what is automated and for seizing the means of production, which overrides private property in them.

state-harmful.rationale: The programme relies on the state to provide universal services, take industries into public hands and run public banks.

limit-growth.rationale: The book rejects the green view that the planet can be saved only by retreating from modernity, and reviewers note it does not countenance reduced consumption or limits on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Bastani says big action is needed to decarbonise the world economy over the next 20 years and sets out how in the book.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Bastani says technologies can remedy crises and create a more civilised society, but also that technology alone, isolated from politics, cannot address social challenges.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Reviewers record that Bastani rejects nuclear power and relies on 100 per cent renewable electricity.

central-planning.rationale: Bastani argues that AI could achieve efficient distribution of goods without recourse to markets and that, if it can outperform markets, the case against planning is moot.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The book proposes national energy investment banks and public banks that steer investment into sustainable energy and housing.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The book explains historical change through technological disruptions and productive forces, and reviewers note that class hardly enters its account.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The book revives ideals of progress, praises capitalism's productive power and rejects the view that people should retreat from modernity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The book says the energy revolution 'must now be accelerated' and that ambitions must be Promethean, and its reviewers read it as accelerationist.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Bastani proposes public investment in cryptography and data anonymisation as fail-safes against state surveillance.

restore-past-order.rationale: The book places its politics in a revival of the ideals of progress and common plenty, and says history moves forward through technology.

direct-action.rationale: Bastani advocates engagement in mainstream electoral politics alongside movements, not replacing it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The book calls the idea that the planet is saved only by retreating from modernity itself unwise and heretical to its own red-green politics of progress.

production-for-use.rationale: Bastani says communism would end production for profit and exchange, and wants societies to pursue care, sustainability and leisure over profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bastani says FALC is not about substituting one class for another, and that it will not be delivered by storming the Winter Palace.

positive-liberty.rationale: Bastani writes that if earth's limits left post-capitalism in abiding scarcity, the realm of freedom would remain out of reach, tying freedom to material abundance.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The programme offers universal services and a guaranteed social wage with no work condition, and aims at a society where work is largely eliminated.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The book calls for an energy revolution that takes humanity beyond the fuels which warmed the planet, and for near-zero emissions in wealthy countries by 2030.

vanguard-party.rationale: The book calls Leninism irrelevant to a changed world, and does not propose a revolutionary vanguard.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bastani builds on Marx's account of productive forces outrunning relations of production, though he adds that ideas, social relations and politics also matter.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The book treats abundant consumption and luxury as the aim, equating luxury with wellbeing, according to its reviewers.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The book's programme ends outsourcing and returns privatised industries to the state, with the public sector displacing outside contractors.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The book joins Marx and Engels in praising capitalism's productive power and treats it as a necessary step before communism, and Bastani admits capitalism has useful features.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Bastani describes his aim as communism, in a post-capitalist society, and rejects capitalism as unable to accept abundance.

free-public-college.rationale: Bastani demands universally guaranteed education, and reviewers describe the book's universal basic services as covering education free to all at the point of use.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The book's path is a reformist government using the existing state for universal services, public ownership and public banks.

simple-living.rationale: FALC promises luxury for all, 'Cartier for everyone' and lives like billionaires, and the book calls the austere green view heretical.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The programme rests on universal basic services provided to everyone, not on schemes limited to the poorest.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Bastani demands full automation of everything and a 10- or 12-hour working week with only minimal human work left.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: The book tells history as a progression through three technological disruptions towards abundance, not as decline.

price-stability-first.rationale: The book would have central banks move away from low inflation towards rising wages, high productivity and affordable house prices.

four-day-week.rationale: Bastani's stated demand is a 10- or 12-hour working week, far below four days.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: The book proposes public bank lending to worker-owned businesses and co-operatives.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Bastani seeks a society in which work is eliminated and labour and leisure blend together, with a 'workers' party against work'.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: The book states that man-made climate change is a crisis of unprecedented magnitude.

automation-leaves-most-without-work.rationale: The book holds that automation will make much of the world's population surplus to economic requirements and that new jobs cannot replace the lost ones.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Bastani says electoral politics alone will not deliver the world he wants but, allied with a constant movement, shapes what is possible, and the book's path runs through a reformist government.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Bastani says selling labour for a wage would no longer be the case and says the long-term aim is a post-work society; the book describes waged work becoming a relic.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Universal basic services, free to all at the point of use, are the centre of the book's programme, and Bastani wants more and more things available to everyone for free or very low cost.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Bastani aims for a post-work society and a 'workers' party against work', which sits against a legal duty to work.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Bastani demands a guaranteed social wage and universally guaranteed housing, education and healthcare.

missingStatements.text: Everyone should be able to live as comfortably as today's wealthiest people.
missingStatements.rationale: Bastani describes FALC as a society where everyone can have the lives of today's billionaires, and says what money buys in London should be available to people in Sunderland or Belfast.

quotes.text: lead lives equivalent – if we so wish – to those of today’s billionaires
If you live in Sunderland or Belfast and you walk through London and see money everywhere, people having fun, there’s no reason that should not be available to you.

notes: Searched every statement theme (economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism) in the reviews of the book, Bastani's Huck, Guardian and Novara texts. The book itself is not freely available, so the record rests on the 2015 Guardian interview, the 2019 Huck interview, a 2021 Novara essay and review quotations with page numbers. Government, world, society and culture themes are largely unaddressed in these sources and stay null. Bastani's preference for universal basic services over a basic income (New Statesman headline, 2023) was seen only in its opening lines, so the basic-income statement stays null. After the validator flagged the nationalism, ethnonationalism, secession and minority-autonomy, monarchy, authoritarianism and secularism lines, additional reviews (Quillette, Theory Culture and Society, Vector, Revolutionary Socialism in the 21st Century, Left Horizons, Commune) and a libcom critique of luxury communism were searched for borders, nationalism, minorities, monarchy, religion, secularism and democracy; none records a position of FALC on them, so they stay null and the uncertainty rule is not met.
